Book correction: The answer key (item 3) prints \sin^{-1}x + \sin^{-1}x + C = 0. This is a misprint: it does not contain y at all, and even with the second term read as \sin^{-1}y the sign would be wrong (\sin^{-1}x + \sin^{-1}y = C solves \frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{\sqrt{1 - y^2}}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}). The correct general solution is \sin^{-1}y - \sin^{-1}x = C.
